investigations.question: When a leader is elected, does it hold the entries up to the decided index it adopts from its read quorum? handle_majority_promises takes the maximum decided index over all promises but the log itself from the single maximum promise metadata, so a promise that reports a decided index covering more entries than that maximum's log could make the adopted decided index exceed the entries the leader holds.
investigations.hypothesis: The adopted decided index can exceed the leader's accepted index whenever the promise with the maximum decided index is not the promise whose log_sync the leader adopts with it (different (n_accepted, accepted_idx) ordering than decided_idx), because sync_log sets the decided index and the log from two independent inputs.
investigations.discriminator: Sample a newly elected leader's decided index against its accepted index and its readable decided log right after its prepare phase, in a history where one promise reports the higher decided index while another promise supplies the log_sync (for example a follower that accepted the StopSign under a later round but reports fewer entries than a promise that decided it).

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds. knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. interpretations.rationale: Five receipts support one index-space confusion and three of its consequences, and the last one shows the defect is not tied to entry configuration. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and receives a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: for a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), for a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), for the leader that took over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and for two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52: accepted 7 over six indices of content, read(5) None, one-element decided read). In every case the replica's own reconfiguration endpoint and decided-log read degrade. (2) A write quorum of inflated reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer indices: the NoSnapshot case (event 24 of the first two receipts) and now the snapshot-enabled case (event 53: accepted 6, decided 7, is_reconfigured false, decided log unreadable), which is the same signature with both entry configurations. (3) The corruption propagates across authority changes: in the newterm/staleleader sequence the follower that re-promised was inflated (event 11) while the new leader and the cut-off node stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10), and after the cut-off node took over it was itself inflated (event 13) with all three nodes at accepted 7 and a one-element decided read (events 12, 14). Controls held in every run: the pre-change samples (events 6-8, 48-50) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 of the first receipt) kept accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true and a six-element decided log for every replica. The registered gap is therefore answered on both halves: the leader-side inflation is witnessed and the snapshot option reproduces rather than avoids the inflation.

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign rather than the reconfiguration or the harness.

The leader-side inflation witness is entangled with the propagation stage: when the cut-off node took over, all three nodes ended at accepted 7 with decided 7 and a one-element decided read (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea events 12-14), so that stage shows the leader's own accepted index exceeded its six indices of content but does not by itself separate its recomputation from the followers' later reports; the isolated single-replica cases (event 35 of the second receipt, event 11 of the third) are the clean witnesses of the resume-point effect.

The leader-side phantom decision requires a write quorum of inflated reporters in one term (two of three nodes); a single inflated follower, or one inflated follower plus a node that received nothing, left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.
limitations: Compaction itself (trim and snapshot calls) was not exercised; only the entry type's use_snapshots() flag differs in the snapshot-enabled run, where the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is evaluated but not entered.

Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the observed producers are explicit reconnected() calls and ordinary leader changes with one node cut off.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes beyond the one newterm/staleleader sequence were not.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.
